provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Ext family batch. Split between same-day emergency repairs and planned door replacements; no door or opener brands named. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: What a snapped torsion spring sounds like, a door that won't lift, frayed cables, a car trapped inside, the emergency release, and why springs aren't a DIY job
pageStructurePlus.why: Most garage door calls start with a bang and a stuck car. A calm page that says what happened and books a same-day visit wins the call.

pageStructurePlus.section: Garage door style gallery by house
pageStructurePlus.contains: Carriage-house, raised panel, flush modern and full-view glass doors, window inserts, wood-look steel, and colours shown on real house styles
pageStructurePlus.why: Replacement buyers choose with their eyes and want to see the door on a house like theirs before they talk price.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Chain, belt and wall-mount jackshaft openers, battery backup, phone control, keypads, quiet operation for rooms above the garage
pageStructurePlus.why: Opener questions come on almost every call. Answering them plainly sells the upgrade without a showroom.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Single, double and triple-layer steel, insulated doors for rooms above or beside the garage, and wind-load doors where local code requires them
pageStructurePlus.why: Insulation and wind rating explain why two doors that look alike carry different prices.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Yearly lubrication, roller, hinge and cable checks, spring balance, photo-eye and auto-reverse safety test, and a plan sign-up
pageStructurePlus.why: Tune-ups catch a worn spring before it snaps and give the company a reason to see every customer once a year.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Rolling steel, sectional commercial and dock doors, high-cycle springs, after-hours repair, and preventive maintenance contracts for property managers
pageStructurePlus.why: Commercial overhead door work recurs and pays on contract. Managers need to see capacity and response times before calling.

designDirections.name: Stuck Door Hotline
designDirections.bestFor: Repair-first garage door companies whose phone rings with broken springs and stuck cars
designDirections.headlineSample: Garage door stuck? Same-day spring repair in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: Amber on obsidian reads like a warning light without panic, and the geometric display keeps the call button huge on a phone in a dark garage.

designDirections.name: New Door, New Front
designDirections.bestFor: Garage door companies balancing repairs with replacement doors and opener upgrades
designDirections.headlineSample: Garage door repair and new doors installed in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: The family's own combo. Evergreen and a refined serif calm the repair caller, and the before-after hero shows how much a new door changes the front of a house.

designDirections.name: Carriage House
designDirections.bestFor: Custom wood and carriage-house garage door installers working with builders and design-led homeowners
designDirections.headlineSample: Custom carriage-house garage doors for {City} homes
designDirections.whyItFits: Olive and a bookish serif feel like a woodshop catalogue, suited to doors sold on grain, hardware and craftsmanship.

openers.line: Your listing has a phone number but no website. When a spring snaps at 7am and the car's trapped, people want to see a garage door company is real and local before they dial.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there's no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: A garage door page for that button: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your website link opens Facebook. Someone picking a new garage door wants to see styles on houses like theirs, and a feed of mixed posts doesn't show that.
openers.hook: Tap their Website link and confirm it lands on Facebook. Note the newest door install posted.
openers.linkLine: A garage door style gallery instead of a feed: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your garage door site still carries a free-host banner and an old year in the footer. A panicked homeowner with a stuck door wonders if the number still works.
openers.hook: Open the site and look for a banner, stale year or broken form. Note which.
openers.linkLine: Same garage door company, current and fast: {demo-link}

openers.angle: Call button hidden on a phone
openers.line: On my phone I had to scroll past three paragraphs to find your number. Garage door emergencies are phone searches, usually standing in the garage.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and time how long the number takes to find. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: A garage door site with the call button where the thumb is: {demo-link}

openers.angle: No way to request a new door
openers.line: For repairs, a call works. For a new garage door, people want to send the opening size and the style they like first, and there's no form for that.
openers.hook: Check the listing and any site for a quote form. If there's none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A new door request that asks size, style and opener: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your new garage door installs on Instagram change the whole front of the house. They're buried between repair clips when a style gallery would sell the next door.
openers.hook: Pick two installs you could name by style and colour. Mention one if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your garage door installs, sorted by style: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews say you fixed a broken spring the same morning and didn't upsell a new door. That's what a stuck homeowner hopes to hear, and it stays on Google.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase about speed or honesty. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Those garage door reviews where callers decide: {demo-link}

openers.line: The first hard freeze is when tired garage door springs give up. The company that shows up first in that morning's search gets the call.
openers.hook: Use ahead of the first cold weather. Name the season in the reply.
openers.linkLine: Ready before the cold-weather spring calls: {demo-link}

openers.line: A garage door that won't close at night means an open house. If the call goes to voicemail, the homeowner tries the next garage door company until someone picks up.
openers.hook: Call their number after hours. If it hits a full or generic voicemail, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A garage door request that works at night: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your hiring post for a garage door tech will send applicants to look you up. A page with your trucks, installs and training says the work is steady.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: A garage door company page with careers: {demo-link}

openers.line: You cover {City} and the towns around it, but nothing tells someone in {Neighborhood} you'll come today. 'Garage door repair' plus the town is the whole search.
openers.hook: Find towns they mention in posts or reviews. Use the furthest one.
openers.linkLine: A garage door page for every town you serve: {demo-link}

openers.line: Every repair visit is a chance to sell a quieter opener with battery backup. A page explaining garage door opener options lets people choose before you arrive.
openers.hook: Only if they post opener installs. Note one.
openers.linkLine: A garage door opener comparison page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Garage door springs carry enough tension to hurt someone, and your licence is on the state registry. Showing it on a page separates you from the spring scammers.
openers.hook: Check the state contractor registry if garage doors are licensed there. Note that a record exists; never quote a number you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Licence and safety on one garage door page: {demo-link}

openers.line: People have heard stories about garage door repair quotes that balloon once the tech arrives. A page with honest spring and cable price ranges is the fastest way to earn their trust.
openers.hook: Look for reviews mentioning fair pricing or 'no upsell'. Quote one back.
openers.linkLine: Honest garage door repair ranges, up front: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted changes the look of the whole house. A garage door job like that should be the first thing visitors see.
openers.hook: Pick their newest install and name it: style, colour, windows, and the street if tagged.
openers.linkLine: That garage door job, front and centre: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner}, that {specific recent job} you posted really changes the front of the house.

I searched for garage door repair in {City} and found {Business Name} on social, but no site with a same-day repair request or a door style gallery. I put together a sample garage door site to see how it would look, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Want me to send it?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, following up in case my message got lost between service calls. Here's the sample garage door site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has a broken-spring help page with a same-day request, honest repair ranges, a door style gallery and an opener comparison. If it's not for you, say so and I'll leave you be.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for garage door companies in {City}. I messaged a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"Easy to miss. Short version: I built a sample site for {Business Name} with a broken-spring page, a same-day repair request and a door style gallery, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I text you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range} depending on how many town and style pages you want, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For a garage door company your size I'd quote about {Build Price}, roughly one new door installed."
"Can I walk you through it for ten minutes, maybe after your last call one day this week?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a short scope and a deposit invoice. It's live before the first cold snap breaks springs."

objections.objection: Most of my calls come from the big paid search ads.
objections.handler: "Those ads are rented. When people click through and find no site, or a weak one, they call the next door company. Your own site makes every ad click land better."

objections.objection: Repair customers just call, they don't browse.
objections.handler: "They don't browse long, but they check. One look at a real local garage door company with reviews and a same-day promise is what makes them call you."

objections.objection: The national garage door chains outspend me.
objections.handler: "They do. People are wary of them too. A local page with honest spring prices and your face is exactly what those people look for."

objections.objection: The manufacturer gives me a dealer page.
objections.handler: "Keep it. That page sells their doors; it doesn't promise same-day repair in your town. Yours does."

objections.objection: My cousin can set something up.
objections.handler: "Fair enough. Happy to hand over the broken-spring page layout. If it stalls before winter, the offer stands."
"{Build Range}. For you, about {Build Price}, for the repair request, honest ranges, a style gallery and a few town pages. About one new door."

email.subject: Garage door site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "Hi {Owner}, {Your Name} here. I build websites for garage door companies in {City} and made a sample for {Business Name} with a same-day repair request. I'll text the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm taking down the {Business Name} garage door demo on Friday.

Want it kept up? One word is fine.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner}, the first cold mornings are close, and that's when worn garage door springs give out. Thought of you.

The site's still here, same price. {demo-link} if you'd like another look.

bullets: Peg the build to one new door installed, not to repair call prices.
Price the same-day repair request and click-to-call setup as the core; it's the reason they'll buy.
The style gallery is a separate line and only worth it for companies that sell replacement doors.
Honest repair ranges are a trust feature; quote them as their own page and confirm the owner is comfortable publishing them.
Commercial door pages only for companies that already service roll-up or dock doors.
Town pages matter more here than in most trades; the search is 'garage door repair' plus a town name.

lineItems.item: Same-day repair request with spring and cable fields
lineItems.description: Max with photo upload, 'car trapped' urgency flag and text alerts to the on-call tech.
Max when filtered by style, colour and window insert, with doors shown on several house types.
Max when it covers springs, cables, rollers, openers and off-track doors with what changes each price.
Max with drive-type comparisons, battery backup and phone-control explainers.
Max when each town page shows local jobs and its typical response time.
Max with a maintenance contract request form and capability list by door type.
Max when the repair request, ranges page and gallery are translated.

whatElseYouSell.name: Garage door install photo morning
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A morning at your three best new garage doors, straight-on and from the street, fills the style gallery and gives you before-and-afters for a year."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, or right after a striking door replacement.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile posts for garage door jobs
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Every week a spring repair or new garage door goes on your Google profile with the town named. In this trade the map listing is where the call starts."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, once the site is live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Review texts after each door visit
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Once the door goes up smoothly and the car's out, the customer gets a text asking for a review. Relief writes the best ones."

whatElseYouSell.name: Local Services Ads for garage door repair
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Garage door repair is a same-day search, and the licence-checked ads sit at the top. I set them up, dispute junk leads and keep them on repair categories."

whatElseYouSell.name: Opener and keypad sticker artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A small sticker on every opener and keypad you touch, with your number and the site, is there the next time a garage door spring snaps."

whatElseYouSell.name: Truck wrap refresh
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Your service truck parks in a different driveway every hour. A clean wrap with 'same-day garage door repair' and the site works the whole route."

whatElseYouSell.name: Fall tune-up campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A fall tune-up offer to past garage door customers catches worn springs before the freeze and fills the quiet weeks."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in August, run in September and October.

whatElseYouSell.name: Builder and realtor door upgrade sheet
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A one-page sheet showing how a new garage door changes curb appeal, for agents prepping listings and builders offering upgrades."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, once the gallery is full.

withoutAI.route: Epoxy floor installers in the same garages
withoutAI.pitchLine: "People who buy a new garage door often coat the floor next. The epoxy crew you know needs a showroom site."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Garage makeovers come in sequence; referrals are natural.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Garage cabinet and overhead rack installers work the same garages as your doors. They need a site, and they send door upgrades back."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Same room, same homeowner, different budget line.

withoutAI.whoPays: The locksmith, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Locksmiths set up keypads and smart locks next to the garage door openers you install. Their site needs the same same-day setup as yours."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Both are emergency trades with overlapping customers.

withoutAI.whoPays: The electrician, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Opener and EV charger installs both need an outlet in the garage. The electrician you call needs a site too."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Electricians are a big referral trade that buys sites.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Managers with townhomes and rental garages get door complaints every week. A tenant request page routes them to your garage door client."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Managers want one dependable vendor and simple requests.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The small builders whose new homes get your garage doors need better sites, and you already meet them on every job."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Builders buy sites and pick door vendors.

withAI.route: Epoxy crew's floor quote from photos
withAI.pitchLine: "The epoxy installer you refer gets a tool that drafts a floor quote from garage photos, and offers a garage door check in the same reply."
"Tenants type 'garage door won't open' and an assistant asks the right questions, marks trapped cars urgent and sends it to one door company."
withAI.whyItWorks: Managers save dispatch time; the garage door client gets steady work.

withAI.pitchLine: "Homeowners upload a garage photo and get a draft cabinet and rack layout, with door clearance and opener rail position checked."
withAI.whyItWorks: Faster designs close storage jobs; door clearance keeps your client involved.

withAI.pitchLine: "Late-night lockout calls get answered and booked, and anything about a stuck garage door goes straight to your client."
withAI.whyItWorks: Both trades lose night calls; sharing the answering helps both.

withAI.route: Builder upgrade selector for garage doors
withAI.pitchLine: "New-home buyers preview garage door styles and opener upgrades on their elevation, and selections route to the builder's door installer."
withAI.whyItWorks: Upgrade revenue for the builder, and the client becomes the default door vendor.

withAI.pitchLine: "Electricians get a tool that drafts an EV charger quote from panel and garage photos, with garage door opener outlets noted."
withAI.whyItWorks: Charger installs are a growing ask; the garage is shared ground.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back for stuck garage doors
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Under a door winding a spring when the phone rings? The caller gets a text asking if the car's trapped and what they heard, so the urgent ones get the first callback."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their number forwarded and approved wording.

softwareAI.name: Tech on-the-way texts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When the garage door tech leaves the last job, the next customer gets a text with a name, a truck photo and an arrival window."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their dispatch list and tech names.

softwareAI.name: Tune-up plan billing and reminders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Tune-up plan members get a reminder each fall and are billed after the visit, so the garage door company sees every customer once a year."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, once the plan page is live. Needs plan prices.

softwareAI.name: Repair price range tool
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A homeowner picks 'loud bang, door won't lift' or 'off track' and sees a fair repair range, which is often what makes them call a garage door company they've never used."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their real repair prices and what changes them.

softwareAI.name: Garage door review reply drafts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A relieved customer posts that you freed their car before work; a short reply naming the spring fix and the tech is waiting for your tap."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, with review texts. Needs a dozen past replies. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Night line for stuck garage doors
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers at eleven at night, walks the caller through the emergency release if it's safe, books a morning slot and only wakes you for trapped cars."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their calendar, after-hours price and safety script. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Door style preview on the customer's house
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Homeowners upload a shot of the front and see new garage door styles, colours and windows on their own house, labelled as a preview."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs the door lines they sell. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Service call board
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every repair call, new door quote, order and install on one board, so a garage door order doesn't sit at the distributor while the customer waits."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their call flow and distributor lead times.

softwareAI.name: Spring and part stock tracker for the trucks
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Know which torsion springs, cables and rollers are on each truck, so the tech fixes the garage door on the first visit instead of coming back."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their parts list and a count per truck.

softwareAI.name: Garage door chatbot for symptoms and openers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'my door goes down then back up' and 'belt or chain opener' at night, from the owner's notes, and books the visit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their symptom notes and opener options. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Door and opener install history by address
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every garage door, spring size and opener installed, saved by address, so the next call starts with the right part on the truck."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs past job records.

softwareAI.name: Symptom photo and video diagnosis
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Customers upload a short clip of the door and it suggests likely causes, spring, cable, roller or opener, so the tech brings the right garage door parts."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs a library of past calls with outcomes. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer; never tells a customer to touch a spring.

softwareAI.name: New door quote builder with opening sizes
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Enter the opening, headroom and style and it prices the new garage door, opener and haul-away in one clean quote."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their door price sheet.

softwareAI.name: Commercial door maintenance tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every roll-up and dock door under contract with its cycle count, last service and next visit, with reports managers can forward."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, once they hold commercial contracts.

softwareAI.name: Spoken service notes to invoice
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The tech says what was replaced on the garage door, springs, cables, rollers, and an invoice draft appears before they leave the driveway."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their parts price list. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Tech performance by call type
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See which garage door techs fix on the first visit, sell openers and earn reviews, so coaching is based on the calls, not hunches."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, with two or more techs. Needs the service call board running.

softwareAI.name: Old-door replacement nudge
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Customers who had a spring repair on an older garage door get a note months later with replacement styles and a quote link."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs repair records marked with door age.

softwareAI.name: Garage door town page writer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A new garage door repair page for a town you serve each month, drafted from jobs there and approved by you."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs job notes and approval. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Customer page with door history and plan
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Customers see their garage door, opener, spring dates and tune-up plan in one place, and book service in a tap."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs install history running.

softwareAI.name: Garage door tech applicant screener
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants say whether they've wound torsion springs, can lift a door section and take on-call nights, before you spend a call."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: When they post a hiring note. Needs their must-haves. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the repair price range tool
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built an honest repair range tool for one garage door company. Every independent in the state fights the same price-gouging reputation."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: A trust problem shared across the trade; one tool fixes it.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Dealer site program for a door manufacturer
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your garage door dealers all run the same thin page. A program that gives each a real site with local repair pages sells more doors."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Manufacturers fund dealer marketing; you know the dealer side.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Installer finder for a garage door distributor
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Homeowners ask the distributor's counter who installs their doors. A searchable installer map answers that and keeps installers ordering."
"Offer member garage door companies a template with a same-day repair request and honest range page."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations can push trust standards across members.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Agencies running paid search for garage door companies need landing pages that convert. License my repair template."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies already sell to this trade heavily.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each garage door territory needs town repair pages and a request form routed to the right owner."
"When an opener fails, owners search for help. A locator that routes them to vetted garage door techs keeps service in the network."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Service requests are lost revenue for the maker today.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Townhome communities with rows of garage doors get one request and maintenance portal, routed to a contracted door company."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Big portfolios buy once and roll out.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Home warranty company door repair network
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Home warranty companies need dependable garage door techs and a clean claim intake. Build the intake and the vetted network page."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Warranty providers struggle to find good door techs.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Monthly spring and opener parts price note
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A short monthly note on spring, cable and opener prices garage door companies report, so repair prices keep up."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Built only from shared data; it never claims more than members report.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A garage door company in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "My garage door clients each get their metro alone. With {City} signed, the most trusted independent door company an hour away is next."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Exclusivity matters in an ad-heavy trade.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Rescue garage door sites tied to ad agencies
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The garage door company leaving an agency
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Garage door owners leaving a pay-per-lead agency often lose the site with it. I rebuild one they own in two weeks."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Owners burned by rented sites buy ownership fast.

upsellLadder.line: "Every missed garage door call is someone else's spring job. A text back keeps them yours."

upsellLadder.offer: Local Services Ads for garage door repair

upsellLadder.line: "Your reviews are strong enough for the licence-checked garage door ads now."

upsellLadder.offer: Night line for stuck garage doors

upsellLadder.line: "Those night calls about doors stuck open are going elsewhere. This answers them."

upsellLadder.trigger: Late summer arrives with open slots in the schedule.
upsellLadder.line: "Let's tune up past customers' garage doors before the freeze snaps their springs."
